idiom_name: typed Promises with async/await (compiled to the ES target)
implementation_notes: TypeScript adds types, not a runtime: Promise<T> is the completion contract, async/await compiles to the chosen ES target (downlevel async has been supported since 2.1), and the dispatch itself is Node's libuv loop or the browser event loop. What TypeScript contributes is making handlers and completion values explicit - typed callbacks, PromiseLike, AsyncIterable and typed wrappers for Node's (err, result) convention - which removes the classic callback-signature mistakes. The classic structure reappears only when wrapping callback APIs with promisify or exposing a callback-shaped API to JavaScript consumers.
pitfalls: A floating promise (not awaited or explicitly void-ed) turns a rejection into an unhandledRejection; enable no-floating-promises.
Typing a Node callback as (result: T) => void silently drops the error parameter; model it as (err: Error | null, result: T) => void or promisify it.
await inside a loop serialises completions that could overlap; use Promise.all or a bounded pool.
